chapter: Louis Armstrong, King Oliver and St. Louis memories
title: First hearing Armstrong in person at the Coliseum
summary: Thomas first heard Armstrong around 1926 at St. Louis's Coliseum, with Carroll Dickerson's band, traveling from Jefferson City on money from his own gigs.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So when did you first hear Pops in person?
Must be around '26.
Oh, yeah. Where?
The Coliseum.
Where, in St. Louis?
In St. Louis.
What was the Coliseum?
The Coliseum, well, they had wrestling and all them kind of things, you know.
Oh, it was a big sort of ...

Oh, yeah, Coliseum, do what it really meant, you know. when Pops worked with Carroll Dickerson And they'd bring Louis's work ... they'd bring in the Cotton- would pickers, they/bring in Henderson. I'll never forget that because I saved enough money to make my round trip fare ... call home and ask for permission.
JT (1 of 2)
Webster Groves still.
No, I'm from Jeff City.
Oh, you'd come all the way down.

Oh, sure. But, you see I made my own little gigs. I had my own money. See what I mean and I got home so often ... don't say, Where is Joe, you know. So, the gigs were coming in pretty fast. I got home damn near every weekend because the food was bad up there. So when I get back home, they'd say Joe, sit down at the table ... I'm home too often. you know,
Well, this Carroll Dickerson band was a big band?
Chicago. Dickerson and ... in Savoy.
That was the first time you saw Louis?
No, no. I saw Louis before Carroll Dickerson.
Oh, you did. Who was he with then?
